messages.author: e59e09508354bebb
messages.subject: finalreport.txt + finalreportmatrixforward.txt file handling
parts:
Dr. Broman,
Any thoughts on handling mixed finalreport.txt files from NeoGen and the like for GigaMUGA data? I've gotten adept at using the DO mice genotype data preparation for typical finalreport.txt files, but there's a matrix-forward batch I'd like to use and am unsure how to accommodate it (if possible)

Something in the 
ifiles <- c("C:/somebigpath/finalreport.txt")
line I assume? Anything up your sleeve would be appreciated!

Best as usual,
Randall 
Cincinnati Childrens Hospital Medical Center

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: finalreport.txt + finalreportmatrixforward.txt file handling
parts:
I don't know what the "matrix-forward batch" data is, but the example of data preparation at https://kbroman.org/qtl2/pages/prep_do_data.html
shows reading two files. In lines 21-22 of the geneseek2qtl2.R file (https://kbroman.org/qtl2/assets/geneseek2qtl2.R) you'll see

ifiles <- c("batch1_FinalReport.txt",
            "batch2_FinalReport.txt")

and then later there is a loop over that vector of files:

for(ifile in ifiles) {
....
}

The finalreport genotype files I've gotten from NeoGen have had some variation in structure, mostly regarding the number of lines in the header, and so the geneseek2qtl2.R file generally needs to be tailored somewhat for the particular data.

karl
